chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

Regarding a slave who injures a free man, he said: “If the free man wishes, he may exact retribution from him; and if he wishes, he may take him, if the wound reaches his neck. But if it does not reach his neck, his master must ransom him. فإذا the master refuses to ransom him, then the injured free man has a share in the slave equal to the diyyah of his injury, and the remainder belongs to the master. The slave is sold, the injured man takes his due, and the remainder is returned to the master.”

key_terms.الْجِرَاحَةُ تُحِيطُ بِرَقَبَتِهِ: an injury severe enough to encompass his neck
key_terms.دِيَةِ جِرَاحَتِهِ: the compensation due for his injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave injures a free man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for when a slave injures a free person. It explains the options of qisas or financial compensation, and clarifies the master's liability and the division of the slave's value according to the amount of the injury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5265 - Imam Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about a slave who injured a free man.
Imam (as) said: "If the free man wishes, he may take retribution (qisas) from him, and if he wishes, he may take the slave if the injury is severe enough to warrant his execution. If the injury does not warrant execution, then the slave's master must pay compensation (diyyah).
If the master refuses to pay the compensation, then the injured free man has a right over the slave equivalent to the diyyah of his injury, and the rest belongs to the master. The slave is then sold, the injured party takes his due, and the remainder is returned to the master."
